narrative:
Based on the information available, the system predicted that there is a 75% chance you may leave your current job. Because this probability is well above the threshold set for promotion decisions, your request for promotion was not approved at this time.

The most influential factor in this prediction was that you reported receiving other job offers while working here. This is less common among employees who were promoted—most did not receive outside offers—which led the system to believe you might be considering opportunities elsewhere. The second most important factor was your extensive experience, with over 11 years in your field. While experience is generally positive, in this context, employees with similar backgrounds sometimes seek new challenges or advancement outside their current organization, which can signal a higher likelihood of leaving. On the other hand, your long tenure of 6 to 10 years with this organization actually worked in your favor, as employees who stay longer in one place are typically seen as more committed. However, this positive influence was outweighed by the other factors.

If you are committed to staying and advancing here, consider discussing your career goals and intentions with your manager. Highlight your loyalty and interest in long-term growth within the company. Addressing any perceptions about your openness to outside opportunities may help clarify your intentions and improve your chances for future promotions.
